title: FRust: the language, for writing scripts
summary: How to write FRust: script shape, blocks and semicolons, values, variables, operators, if, loops, functions, structs, enums and match, and what FRust does not have.

blocks.text: FRust looks like Rust but is a different, smaller language. Do not assume Rust rules; use what is written here. Every example on this page was compiled against the real compiler.

blocks.definition: Whole numbers are i64 (3, -2). Decimals are f64 and are written with a point (-6.0, 0.5). Text is String, in double quotes, with \n \t \\ and \" as escapes. Truth values are bool (true, false). A list is [1, 2, 3], all items the same kind.

FRust has NO string concatenation, NO formatting, NO macros such as format! or println!, and NO methods on values (no .to_string(), .len()). To report a number call station_log_i64 or station_log_f64; to report text call station_log or return it.

NEVER compare text with == or !=: that compares where the texts are stored, not their characters, so it is always wrong and the compiler rejects it. Use text_equals(a, b), text_equals_ignore_case(a, b), text_starts_with(a, b), text_ends_with(a, b) and text_contains(a, b), which give true or false; text_compare(a, b), which gives -1, 0 or 1; and text_length(a). Example: if (text_equals(station_track_name(track), "Bass")) { ... }. Comparison is by character; the ignore-case form treats A-Z and a-z as the same.

Arithmetic + - * / %; comparison == != < > <= >=; bitwise & | ^ << >>; negation -x; not !x; cast x as f64. There is NO && and NO ||. To test two things, nest the if blocks, or combine parenthesized comparisons with & (and) or | (or).

blocks.text: Always put the condition of `if` and `while` in parentheses. A bare name before `{` is read as the start of a struct value and fails to compile: write `if (ok) { ... }`, never `if ok { ... }`.

match arms are NOT separated by commas. Each arm is `pattern => expression`, optionally followed by `;`, and the last arm has none. The value being matched is in parentheses: `match (n) { ... }`. Every arm must give the same kind of value.

Comments start with // and run to the end of the line, or sit between /* and */. FRust also has effects, smart pointers (own, shared, weak, raw*), refinement types and quote/unquote; scripts for Station rarely need them.
